newsitem.title: BELGIUM: France's Strauss-Kahn says sticks to EMU timetable.
newsitem.headline: France's Strauss-Kahn says sticks to EMU timetable.

text.p: French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said on Monday all European Union states must try to be ready to launch economic and monetary union (EMU) as scheduled in 1999, a date France was committed to.

"We must all get ourselves into a position to be able to stick to the January 1, 1999 date," Strauss-Kahn told a news conference at a meeting of European Union finance ministers in Brussels. "I am committed to sticking to the date."
Strauss-Kahn said that EMU should help in Europe's fight against unemployment, not hinder it. "The existence of the euro is favourable to employment," he said.
France's Socialist-led government is under pressure from coalition partners to maintain employment at the top of its agenda after being swept to power in June on a job-creating platform.
The government is however already finding it difficult to balance pre-election promises, such as creating 700,000 new work places, with the task of getting its budget in order for EMU.
French premier Lionel Jospin said in a television last week that he could not move forward on potentially costly programmes until an audit of public finances was completed on July 21.
